spec_match.rationale: Multicol is the right showcase per the ChromeStatus scope, but the page's central claim — that without margin-trim 'every column keeps its top margin' — is contradicted by its own measurements on this browser: CSS fragmentation already truncates margins adjoining column breaks, so columns 2+ measured 0px (flush) with no margin-trim at all.

interactive.rationale: Column and item sliders, a margin-trim toggle and Re-measure rebuild the flow and a per-column measured table that groups items by rendered column.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index sells 'the first element in every column needs the trim', which the break-margin truncation the page itself measures makes at best half-true — the untrimmed gap that actually persists is at the container's own block-start edge (column 1).

edge_cases.rationale: Column/item counts and the unsupported branch are covered, but the case the narration is really about (margins surviving a column break) never occurs, and the narration does not notice.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves block-container behaviour well but contains no multicol assertion, so the one scenario this page exists for is unpinned — and the suite's inline assertions are separately flagged (see trim-explorer critique).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: with trim on or off the table read column 1 = 16px 'margin remains', columns 2-3 = 0px 'flush'; at 4 columns the narration claimed 'every one keeping a 16px margin above its first item' directly above a table showing three flush columns; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Renders log and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('multicol-measured', …) with columns, trim state and flush count.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, good/bad cells pair colour with text, amber padding band, 44px controls.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled sliders and checkbox, captioned per-column table with scoped headers, aria-live narration.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; both screenshots clean.

openQuestions.title: Reconcile the narration with break-margin truncation — the measurements already disagree with it
openQuestions.detail: css-break truncates margins adjoining an unforced fragmentation break, and this page's own table shows it: on Chromium 141 with NO margin-trim support, columns 2+ measure 0px above their first item while the unsupported-branch narration says '4 columns, every one keeping a 16px margin above its first item — including the columns whose first item is in the middle of the source order'. That sentence is false against the table directly above it (misleading-copy defect class). The honest multicol story is narrower and still good: the container's own block-start edge (column 1) keeps the margin that no selector-based reset can express per-column, and margin-trim: block removes it. Rewrite the narrations (all three branches) from the measured groups — e.g. count only columns whose gap is nonzero — and consider showing the css-break truncation explicitly as a labelled observation, since it is half of why the layout looks the way it does. Verify the supported branch on Chrome 155 while at it.

openQuestions.title: Add a multicol assertion to the conformance suite (new assertion, additive)
openQuestions.detail: Nothing in v155/margin-trim/conformance.json exercises a multicol container, so the scenario this concept page exists for has no immutable contract. An additive assertion (column-1 first-item gap goes to zero under margin-trim: block in a column-count container) would pin it; adding new assertions is allowed, editing existing ones is not.

summary: Right scenario, wrong narration: the interactive machinery, per-column measurement and honest unsupported banner all work (verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless — cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp — at http://localhost:3000/v155/margin-trim/multicol/ with clean console and no overflow on either class), but the page's story assumes column-top margins survive without margin-trim, and its own table proves they do not — fragmentation truncation already zeroes columns 2+ here, leaving only column 1 at 16px. The narration contradicting the adjacent measurement is the defect to fix; the demo underneath is sound. Feature /conformance/ route ran 0 pass / 7 fail (honest pre-155 gaps; no multicol assertion exists).
